page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.6xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 architecture, specifically the Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core execution, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, falls into the bottom 25% tier, with single-threaded compression tasks like gzip and bzip3 ranking in the bottom 10%. However, the 24 dedicated cores deliver average multi-core performance, as evidenced by middle-tier ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached reads and writes also align with average performance tiers, though the overall PassMark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g5.6xlarge offers a standard general-purpose resource density without the premium associated with high-frequency compute or massive memory-optimized configurations. The instance is suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage the 24 dedicated cores to offset the lower single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and moderate Redis deployments, whereas single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM inference tasks may experience performance bottlenecks.

This profile makes the ecs.g5.6xlarge qualitatively cost-efficient for parallelized, multi-threaded workloads. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, multi-threaded decompression, and database operations that benefit from dedicated core allocation without requiring high single-thread speeds.
